welcomeAllowanceFailed.message: $ERROR$ The plan size is saved, but the warnings are not set up — try again from Settings.
welcomeAllowanceFailed.description: Status under the plan form when the plan size was stored but the allowance behind it was not. Named rather than swallowed: this is the one state where the product looks set up and no warning can ever arrive.

welcomeAllowanceFailedFallback.description: Used as the $ERROR$ part of welcomeAllowanceFailed when the failure carried no message of its own.

welcomeCycleDayCalendar.description: First option in the reset-day picker: the cycle is the calendar month.

welcomeCycleDayLabel.description: Label of the picker for the day of the month the data plan rolls over.

welcomeCycleDayOption.description: Every other option in the reset-day picker, running from the 2nd to the 28th. DAY is an ordinal built from the welcomeOrdinal* messages.

welcomeCycleHint.description: Hint under the reset-day picker, giving the chosen day as the two dates a person can check against a bill.

welcomeIntro.message: Byte Budget is already counting. Answering these turns a running total into a position — on track, or not. All of it is optional; skip it and nothing breaks.
welcomeIntro.description: Standfirst under welcomeTitle. Says measurement has already started, so the page is not a setup gate.

welcomeNavDashboard.description: Link at the foot of the first-run page, opening the full dashboard.

welcomeNavLabel.description: Accessible name of the link row at the foot of the first-run page.

welcomeNavSettings.description: Link at the foot of the first-run page, opening the settings page.

welcomeOrdinalFew.description: Ordinal form used in English for days ending in 3 but not 13: 3rd, 23rd.

welcomeOrdinalOne.description: Ordinal form used in English for days ending in 1 but not 11: 1st, 21st. Which of the four welcomeOrdinal* forms is chosen still follows English rules, so a locale with different ordinal categories needs that selection changed as well.

welcomeOrdinalOther.description: Ordinal form used in English for every other day: 4th, 11th, 12th, 13th, 20th.

welcomeOrdinalTwo.description: Ordinal form used in English for days ending in 2 but not 12: 2nd, 22nd.

welcomePageTitle.description: Document title of the first-run page, shown in the browser tab. 'Byte Budget' is the product name and is not translated.

welcomePinBody.message: Day to day, Byte Budget is a button on the toolbar. Chrome starts new extensions hidden: open the puzzle-piece icon to the right of the address bar, find Byte Budget in the list, and press the pin beside it to keep the button on the toolbar.
welcomePinBody.description: How to pin the extension. Describes Chrome's own interface, so the wording has to keep matching it — the puzzle-piece icon opens the extensions menu and each entry carries a pin control.

welcomePinFallback.message: Nothing depends on pinning it. The dashboard and settings are always reachable from that menu, and from Chrome's extensions page.
welcomePinFallback.description: Second paragraph of the pin panel, so the instruction reads as convenience rather than a required step. Byte Budget measures whether or not its button is visible.

welcomePinTitle.description: Heading of the panel telling the user how to keep Byte Budget's toolbar button visible. Chrome hides a newly installed extension's button behind the puzzle-piece menu, and the button is the surface the extension is used from.

welcomePlanDetailsAllowance.message: The size becomes an allowance over everything you browse, and that allowance is what the warnings are measured against. They arrive at 75%, 90% and 100%. Those three are fixed; there is no fourth.
welcomePlanDetailsAllowance.description: First paragraph of welcomePlanDetailsSummary: what the number is used for.

welcomePlanDetailsEnforcement.message: Nothing is refused below 100%. At 100% Byte Budget starts refusing subresources — images, video, scripts — on every site until the allowance rolls over. The page itself always loads, carrying a banner that says why. Change the allowance, pause it for an hour, or remove it entirely in Settings.
welcomePlanDetailsEnforcement.description: Second paragraph of welcomePlanDetailsSummary: what actually gets refused, and every way back out of it.

welcomePlanDetailsResetDay.message: Reset days stop at the 28th because every month has one. A cycle anchored to the 31st would reset on a different date in February, and the reset date is the one figure here you check against a bill.
welcomePlanDetailsResetDay.description: Third paragraph of welcomePlanDetailsSummary: why the reset-day picker stops at 28.

welcomePlanDetailsSummary.description: Summary of the collapsed block under the plan form, which spells out the consequences of pressing Save.

welcomePlanSave.description: Submit button of the plan form. Nothing on this page is written until it is pressed.

welcomePlanSaveFailed.description: Status under the plan form when the background worker refuses the settings write.

welcomePlanSaveUnreadable.message: Could not read "$INPUT$" as a size. Try 15 GB, or leave it blank.
welcomePlanSaveUnreadable.description: Status under the plan form when Save is pressed on a size the parser cannot read. Nothing is written and focus returns to the field.

welcomePlanSaved.message: Saved. $SIZE$ a month, next reset $RESET$. Change it any time in Settings.
welcomePlanSaved.description: Status under the plan form after a successful save, repeating back both figures.

welcomePlanSavedNone.message: Saved. No plan set — usage is measured all the same, and you can set one in Settings later.
welcomePlanSavedNone.description: Status under the plan form after saving with the size left blank, which also clears any allowance already stored.

welcomePlanSizeBlank.message: Blank is fine. Usage is still measured — there is just nothing to measure it against.
welcomePlanSizeBlank.description: Hint under the allowance field while it is empty.

welcomePlanSizeLabel.description: Label of the field where the user types their monthly data allowance.

welcomePlanSizePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the allowance field, showing the format expected. Must stay a size the app's own parser reads back: a number, then one of B, kB, MB, GB, TB or KiB, MiB, GiB, TiB. A bare number is read as megabytes.

welcomePlanSizeRead.description: Hint under the allowance field, echoing back the size the parser actually took. A bare number means megabytes and a comma means different things in different locales, so a figure read as ten times what was typed has to be visible before it is saved.

welcomePlanSizeUnreadable.message: Could not read "$INPUT$". Try 15 GB, 500 MB or 20 GiB.
welcomePlanSizeUnreadable.description: Hint under the allowance field when the parser cannot tell what was typed. The three examples must stay sizes the parser reads.

welcomePlanSizeZero.message: A plan of nothing is not a plan. Leave it blank instead.
welcomePlanSizeZero.description: Hint under the allowance field when the typed size parses to zero.

welcomePlanTitle.message: How big is your plan, and when does it reset?
welcomePlanTitle.description: Heading of the plan panel, and the accessible name of the region. A screen reader announces this on entering, with none of the surrounding page for context, so it names the whole question.

welcomeSaverChangeFailed.description: Status under the Data Saver switch when a change fails to save. The switch is re-read from storage rather than left showing the value that was refused.

welcomeSaverControl.message: To measure what that saves rather than estimate it, about one page load in ten is deliberately left unoptimized as a control.
welcomeSaverControl.description: Discloses the holdout: the product deliberately does not optimize a sample of page loads so the saving can be measured rather than modelled.

welcomeSaverIntro.message: Asks sites for less, so a page costs fewer bytes to open: a smaller version of the same picture from known image services, no analytics beacons, and no pre-buffering of video that is off screen. The individual features, per-site exceptions and the off switch are all in Settings.
welcomeSaverIntro.description: What Data Saver does, plus where to change or undo it. The first clause is the outcome and the rest is the mechanism, in that order: this is the first description of the product's main feature anyone reads, and it used to open on "known image CDNs" — the whole sentence was true and the first four words were jargon. Nothing was dropped; the same three behaviours are still named.

welcomeSaverKicker.description: Kicker above the Data Saver heading, marking the panel as skippable.

welcomeSaverOff.message: Data Saver is off. No request is being rewritten or refused.
welcomeSaverOff.description: Status under the Data Saver switch while it is off.

welcomeSaverOn.message: Data Saver is on for every site. Switch it off with this control, or exclude one site in Settings.
welcomeSaverOn.description: Status under the Data Saver switch while it is on. States the way back out, not a benefit.

welcomeSaverReadFailed.description: Status under the Data Saver switch when its current state cannot be read from the background worker.

welcomeSaverSwitchLabel.description: Visible label of the on/off switch in the Data Saver panel. Same words as welcomeSaverTitle but a control label rather than a heading, so it is kept separate.

welcomeSaverTitle.description: Heading of the Data Saver panel, and the accessible name of the region. 'Data Saver' is the product's name for its set of page optimizers.

welcomeSaving.description: Status shown while a save is in flight, under the plan form and under the Data Saver switch.

welcomeScopeBody.message: Everything Byte Budget counts happens inside this Chrome profile. A second profile, a different browser, apps outside Chrome, system and app updates, and every other device sharing your connection are invisible to an extension — there is no API that would show them — so a carrier’s figure can sit well above this one, sometimes by a factor of several. None of what it counts is uploaded. If you later connect a Plus account, its status is checked separately with ExtensionPay and no usage or site name is sent.
welcomeScopeBody.description: The scope paragraph. Says plainly that a carrier's bill will read higher than this and why, so the difference is not read later as a defect.

welcomeScopeTitle.message: What these numbers do not cover
welcomeScopeTitle.description: Heading of the panel bounding what the extension can and cannot see.

welcomeSettingsReadFailed.message: Could not read the current settings.
welcomeSettingsReadFailed.description: Status under the plan form when the page cannot load the stored plan to prefill the fields.

welcomeSkip.description: Button that closes the first-run tab without writing anything. The install is already working on its defaults.

welcomeTitle.message: Two questions, then it runs on its own
welcomeTitle.description: Main heading of the first-run page. The two questions are the plan size and the reset day; nothing else on the page is required.
